reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the general redox buffering capacity of CeO₂ and its facet-dependent reducibility, but it does not provide any specific prior evidence for the key premises that ALD of a sub-monolayer CeO₂ on multi-element alloy catalysts prevents sintering, avoids active-site occlusion, or improves durability under the specified automotive exhaust conditions.
premises: CeO₂ provides redox buffering via reversible Ce⁴⁺/Ce³⁺ cycling and oxygen vacancies
CeO₂ can prevent sintering and deactivation of supported metal nanoparticles
ALD can deposit a conformal, ultrathin CeO₂ layer on catalyst particles
A sub-monolayer CeO₂ coating will not occlude active sites while still providing the protective/redox functions
The CeO₂ coating will maintain low-temperature activity and durability under transient exhaust conditions with H₂O and NO
